beats.text: In 1861, Harriet Colfax took charge of Michigan City's lighthouse. She kept the light burning for 43 years.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY, INDIANA

beats.text: She lived in the lighthouse with her lifelong companion, Ann Hartwell.
beats.label: HARRIET AND ANN

beats.text: In 1871, a pier light was added. Through 1882, five assistant keepers served with her: two women and three men.
beats.label: 1871: A SECOND LIGHT

beats.text: In 1873, she wrote in her log: A terrible hurricane tonight.
beats.label: HER LOG, 1873
beats.credit: National Park Service; Indiana State Library

beats.text: Until a storm took the pier light in 1886, she tended it too, even when waves broke over the walkway and ice coated it.
beats.label: THE PIER LIGHT, 1871-1886
beats.credit: National Park Service; Indiana State Library; Lighthousefriends

beats.text: Harriet retired in 1904, at about 80. That year, she said she could not bear to see anyone else light her lamp. She died the next spring.
beats.credit: Lighthousefriends; Indiana State Library; National Park Service

lines: I could not bear to see

beats.text: Her 1858 lighthouse still stands. Today, it's a museum.
beats.label: THE OLD LIGHTHOUSE
beats.credit: Michigan City Historical Society; Lighthousefriends; Indiana Landmarks
